text.p: Hungary's OTP Securities rated the shares in drug company Egis as "hold" in the short term and "buy" in the long term, saying the company has limited growth potential on the domestic market but has better prospects in eastern Europe.

"Egis's share prices are expected to grow at a slower pace than the sector average because the company will see only slight growth in its domestic market," OTP Securities' analysts Gabor Korondan and Zoltan Kurali said in a report.
The analysts said that financial problems in Hungary's healthcare system will have a negative impact on the pharmaceuticals market.

Nevertheless, they added, "the pharmaceuticals sector is one of Hungary's economic success stories and Egis is a premier pharmaceuticals firm." "We therefore suggest 'hold' in the short term," they said.
OTP Securities was bullish on the long-term outlook of Egis, in which France's Servier S.A. acquired a 51 percent stake in late 1995.
"Egis has good long-term prospects," Korondan and Kurali said. "As its generic products break into western markets, the alliance with Servier will serve it well."

Egis, whose domestic sales account for around half of its total sales -- thus it is more exposed to the local market than peer firm Richter whose sales here account for around one-third of total -- also focuses on east European markets.

"Egis is currently developing its network in eastern Europe, positioning it to reap the reward as this market begins to expand," the analysts said, forecasting a substantial improvement in Egis' sales in 1998.
OTP Securities predicts the pharmaceuticals company's sales rising to 29.60 billion forints in 1997 and 35.19 billion forints in 1998, up from an estimated 24.57 billion this year.
"We therefore rate Egis a 'long-term buy'," they said.
